questions.question: How do conditionals and loops work in Ruby?
questions.title: Conditionals and Loops in Ruby
questions.direct_answer: Conditionals: if/elsif/else/end (if x > 0 ... elsif x == 0 ... else ... end), unless (unless done ... end — opposite of if), and the modifier form (puts 'hi' if x > 0). case/when for multi-way (case x; when 1..5 then 'small'; when String then 'str'; else 'other'; end). Loops: while (while i < 10 ... i += 1; end), until (until done ... end), and the idiomatic iterators (10.times { |i| ... }, array.each { |x| ... }, 1.upto(5) { |n| ... }). In Ruby you almost never write while — you use each/times/upto/map over collections. break exits a loop; next skips to the next iteration; redo retries the current. Loop with iterators, not counters, whenever you can.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know if/unless/case and that Ruby prefers iterators (each/times/upto) over while counters.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using a while counter when each/times would do (un-idiomatic), or confusing unless with if (unless = if not).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Conditionals: if/elsif/else, unless (if not), case/when. Loops: while/until, but prefer iterators (each/times/upto). break/next/redo.

sections.title: Branch and Iterate
sections.content: Conditionals: if, elsif, else, end (if x greater than 0 dot dot dot elsif x equals 0 dot dot dot else dot dot dot end), unless (unless done dot dot dot end, opposite of if), and the modifier form (puts hi if x greater than 0). case when for multi-way (case x; when 1 to 5 then small; when String then str; else other; end). Loops: while (while i less than 10 dot dot dot i plus 1; end), until (until done dot dot dot end), and the idiomatic iterators (10 dot times block i dot dot dot, array dot each block x dot dot dot, 1 dot upto 5 block n dot dot dot). In Ruby you almost never write while — you use each, times, upto, map over collections. break exits a loop; next skips to the next iteration; redo retries the current. Loop with iterators, not counters, whenever you can.

sections.title: Conditionals + Loops
sections.content:
if/elsif/else, unless, case/when; while/until, but prefer each/times/upto. break/next/redo.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[conditionals] --> I[if/elsif/else]
  C --> U[unless: if not]
  C --> Ca[case/when]
  L[loops] --> W[while/until]
  L --> It[iterators: each/times/upto]
```

sections.title: Conditionals and loops
sections.content:
```ruby
# Conditionals
if score > 90
  'A'
elsif score > 80
  'B'
else
  'C'
end

puts 'done' unless running   # unless = if NOT
puts 'hi' if verbose         # modifier form

case x
when 1..5      then 'small'   # range
when String    then 'string'  # class check
when 'a', 'b'  then 'letter'  # multiple
else 'other'
end

# Loops
i = 0
while i < 3
  puts i; i += 1
end
until done
  do_stuff
end

# PREFER iterators (idiomatic Ruby):
3.times { |i| puts i }            # 0 1 2
[10, 20].each { |x| puts x }       # 10 20
1.upto(5) { |n| puts n }           # 1..5
nums.map { |n| n * 2 }             # transform

# break (exit), next (skip), redo (retry current)
[1,2,3].each do |n|
  next if n == 2      # skip 2
  break if n > 10      # stop
end
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Using a while counter when each/times would do (un-idiomatic).
Confusing unless with if (unless = if NOT).
Forgetting end on if/case/while blocks (Ruby uses end, not braces).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Conditionals: if/elsif/else/end, unless (= if not), and case/when (range/class).
Loops: while/until, but Ruby prefers iterators (each/times/upto/map).
The modifier form: puts 'hi' if x > 0 (condition after the statement).
break exits a loop; next skips to the next iteration; redo retries the current.
Loop with iterators, not counters, whenever you can (idiomatic Ruby).

Loops: while (while i less than 10 dot dot dot i plus 1; end), until (until done dot dot dot end), and the idiomatic iterators (10 dot times block i dot dot dot, array dot each block x dot dot dot, 1 dot upto 5 block n dot dot dot). In Ruby you almost never write while — you use each, times, upto, map over collections. break exits a loop; next skips to the next iteration; redo retries the current.
